definition: Stolid means showing little feeling by temperament, whatever churns underneath.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word stolid. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know stolid should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Through wins, losses, and a bench-clearing brawl, the pitching coach stayed stolid, arms crossed in the same corner of the dugout.
Matter-of-fact is milder than stolid: a matter-of-fact nurse delivers the news plainly but can still smile on the way out, while a stolid one shows almost no feeling at all.
Expressionless goes further than matter-of-fact—an expressionless face is a blank wall showing nothing at all, while a stolid one still leaks the occasional shrug.

Unemotional is the plain umbrella word for feeling kept off the face—it can cover one moment or a whole lifetime, a person or a policy. Stolid is the temperament version: someone who by nature rarely shows feeling, whatever churns underneath. Every stolid person reads as unemotional; one unemotional moment does not make anyone stolid.

Deadpan is blankness on purpose, usually for effect—a comedian delivering the punch line with a perfectly straight face. Stolid blankness is not a performance; it is simply how the face rests. Deadpan invites you to notice the mask; a stolid face does not know it is wearing one.
